proposals.premise: The three dated records invite chronological comparison. Grocery-label comparison and sorting household bills both align unlike items by one shared field before opening details; dates map to the spine, items to records, and labels to source notes.
proposals.opening: Desktop shows a horizontal 1932–2025 sequence beside one selected record; phone stacks the same sequence above it. Media, transcript access, source and uncertainty share the detail area.
proposals.move: Select a dated record; its media opens in place, with links to the other two and visible provenance notes.
proposals.tradeoff: Time relationships become immediate, but the east abutment and public steps remain secondary context.

proposals.premise: Assume visitors may know the present bend better than its dates. Airport wayfinding and hardware-store aisle signs start from recognizable places, then reveal destinations; the public steps and east abutment map to place anchors, while the ferry photo remains explicitly tied to a changed bend.
proposals.opening: Desktop presents two place labels and a ferry-era section beside a record pane; phone shows those labels first, with the selected record directly below. Sources and uncertainty stay alongside each item.
proposals.move: Choose a place label; matching records appear below, where the audio can play or its transcript can replace the player.
proposals.tradeoff: Local relevance improves, but chronology requires an extra switch to compare all three dates.
